info.description:
Documentation of Armo Platform API
How to get the API key
Get the API key from the Armo platform
  1. Navigate to the https://cloud.armosec.io
  2. Click on Settings (bottom left corner)
  3. Under the Agent Access Keys section, generate a new access key or use an existing one.
  4. Copy and save the access key, as it will not appear again.
Using the API Key in Requests
Pass the access key in the request headers under the key x-api-key as shown below:

curl -X 'POST' \
 'https://api.armosec.io/api/v1/some-endpoint' \
 -H 'accept: application/json' \
 -H 'x-api-key: YOUR_ACCESS_KEY' \
 -d '{}'

post.description:
Creates a new runtime policy for monitoring and responding to security incidents.
The policy defines which alerts to act on (via rules/incident types), which resources
to monitor (via scope designators), and what to do when a match occurs (notifications + actions).

### Query params
`customerGUID` - required. Unique identifier for the customer.

### Validation rules
`name` is mandatory.
`ruleSetType` must be "Managed" or "Custom".
If `ruleSetType` is "Managed", `managedRuleSetIDs` must be non-empty.
`incidentTypeIDs` and `managedRuleSetIDs` are mutually exclusive.
If notifications include Slack, `slackChannel.channelID` is mandatory.
If `sensorPlatform` is set, it must be a positive integer: 1 (K8sAgent), 2 (HostAgent), 3 (Cloud), 4 (ECSAgent), 5 (PtraceAgent).
If both `sensorPlatform` and `service` are set, they must be consistent: CDR requires platform 3, ADR requires any non-Cloud platform.

### Scope semantics
Multiple designators are OR'd — the policy matches if ANY designator matches the alert.
Fields within a single designator are AND'd — ALL non-null fields must match.
Omitted (null) fields act as wildcards — they match any value.

### Designator fields by platform

#### ADR (K8s workloads):
 Field | Description | Example |
-------|-------------|---------|
 service | Service type | "ADR" |
 sensorPlatform | Platform ID (int) | 1 (K8sAgent) |
 cluster | K8s cluster name | "prod-cluster" |
 namespace | K8s namespace | "default" |
 kind | Workload kind | "Deployment" |
 name | Workload name | "payment-api" |
 labels | Label filter (key:value) | "env:production" |

#### ADR (Host):
 Field | Description | Example |
-------|-------------|---------|
 service | Service type | "ADR" |
 sensorPlatform | Platform ID (int) | 2 (HostAgent) |
 cloudProvider | Cloud provider | "aws" |
 accountID | Cloud account | "123456789012" |
 region | Cloud region | "us-east-1" |
 instanceID | Host instance ID | "i-0abc123def456" |

#### CDR (Cloud):
 Field | Description | Example |
-------|-------------|---------|
 service | Service type | "CDR" |
 sensorPlatform | Platform ID (int) | 3 (Cloud Log Agent) |
 cloudProvider | Cloud provider | "aws" |
 accountID | Cloud account | "123456789012" |
 region | Cloud region | "eu-west-1" |

### Notification types

#### Slack:
```json
{ "provider": "slack", "slackChannel": { "channelID": "C0123ABCDEF" } }
```

#### Teams:
```json
{ "provider": "teams", "teamsWebhookURL": "https://outlook.office.com/webhook/..." }
```

#### Webhook:
```json
{ "provider": "webhook", "webhookChannel": { "guid": "...", "name": "...", "webhookURL": "https://..." } }
```

### Request examples

#### ADR policy — K8s workload + Host (mixed scope):
```json
{
"name": "Production ADR Policy",
"description": "Monitors K8s workloads and EC2 hosts",
"enabled": true,
"ruleSetType": "Custom",
"incidentTypeIDs": ["I006", "I007", "I008", "I010", "I011"],
"scope": {
"designators": [
{
"service": "ADR",
"sensorPlatform": 1,
"cluster": "prod-cluster",
"namespace": "payments",
"kind": "Deployment",
"name": "payment-api",
"labels": "env:production"
},
{
"service": "ADR",
"sensorPlatform": 2,
"cloudProvider": "aws",
"accountID": "123456789012",
"region": "us-east-1",
"instanceID": "i-0abc123def456"
},
{
"service": "ADR",
"sensorPlatform": 1,
"cluster": "staging-cluster",
"labels": "team:backend"
}
]
},
"notifications": [],
"actions": [],
"applyNetworkPolicy": false,
"applySeccompProfile": false
}
```

#### CDR policy — Cloud accounts:
```json
{
"name": "AWS Cloud Monitoring",
"description": "CDR for AWS production accounts",
"enabled": true,
"ruleSetType": "Custom",
"incidentTypeIDs": ["I001", "I002"],
"scope": {
"designators": [
{
"service": "CDR",
"sensorPlatform": 3,
"cloudProvider": "aws",
"accountID": "123456789012",
"region": "us-east-1"
},
{
"service": "CDR",
"sensorPlatform": 3,
"cloudProvider": "aws",
"accountID": "123456789012",
"region": "eu-west-1"
}
]
},
"notifications": [
{
"provider": "slack",
"slackChannel": { "channelID": "C0123ABCDEF" }
}
],
"actions": [],
"applyNetworkPolicy": false,
"applySeccompProfile": false
}
```

#### Managed policy:
```json
{
"name": "Default ADR Ruleset",
"enabled": true,
"ruleSetType": "Managed",
"managedRuleSetIDs": ["<ruleset-guid>"],
"scope": {
"designators": []
},
"notifications": [],
"actions": [],
"applyNetworkPolicy": false,
"applySeccompProfile": false
}
```

ProfileDataField.description:
ProfileDataField is a tagged union: either All == true (the rule needs every
entry on this surface) or Patterns is non-empty (the rule needs entries
matching any pattern). The YAML/JSON form is either the literal string "all"
or a list of ProfileDataPattern objects.

ProfileDataPattern.description:
ProfileDataPattern declares a single match pattern for a profile-data
surface. Exactly one of the four fields must be non-empty.

ProfileDataRequired.description:
ProfileDataRequired declares which subsets of the container profile this rule
needs at runtime. Each surface field is optional; absence means "this rule
does not query this surface".
